prompt.context_jp: 新しい年を迎える夜、新島家の茶の間には久しぶりに家族の笑い声___満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家族の笑い声___満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the opening description of the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is introducing a scene the reader hasn't yet seen — laughter newly filling the room. New, descriptive information presented as a whole event takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 笑い声 as an already-established topic, which clashes with this fresh scene-setting line. を can't mark the subject of 満ちる (an intransitive verb).

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に光が差し込んだ。
contrast_examples.en: Light streamed into the room. (newly perceived event — が)
That light was warm. (now a known topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 騒ぎのさなか、新しい人物が現れる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 座敷の奥から寺の主人___静かに歩み寄ってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces this newly appearing character?

feedback.correct_en: The temple master enters the scene here for the first time — a new participant is introduced with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that 寺の主人 is already an established topic, but he's just now walking into frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 廊下から男が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: A man came in from the hallway. (first appearance — が)

contrast_examples.jp: その男は寺の主人だった。
contrast_examples.en: That man was the temple master. (now topicalized — は)

prompt.context_jp: 寺の主人が心配する圭介をなだめている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大丈夫 じき 目___覚めるわよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside this reassurance?

feedback.correct_en: 目が覚める is a fixed subject-predicate pair where 目 is the thing that will spontaneously happen — the subject of an intransitive event takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 目 into a contrastive topic (as for her eyes...), which is odd. を would require a transitive verb like 覚ます (目を覚ます).

contrast_examples.en: She'll wake up soon. (intransitive — が)
She woke herself up. (transitive — を)

prompt.context_jp: 小さな身体に貴恵の口調が宿っていることを地の文が描写する。
prompt.prompt_jp: ちいさな身体に不釣り合いなその物言い___、昔と少しも変わらない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this topic-comment sentence?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator picks up 'that way of speaking' as the theme and comments on it ('hasn't changed at all'). Topic-plus-comment structure takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the way of speaking as newly-introduced information, but the whole sentence is a reflection on something already evoked by the preceding scene.

contrast_examples.jp: その口調は昔のままだ。
contrast_examples.en: That way of speaking is just as it was. (topic — は)

contrast_examples.jp: どこかで聞いた口調がする。
contrast_examples.en: I hear a tone from somewhere. (new perception — が)

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣が友利に大晦日の出来事を打ち明けている最中。
prompt.prompt_jp: 話___進むにつれ、友利の顔からは正月気分の締まりのなさが消えていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle belongs inside this subordinate clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜につれ subordinate clause, the subject is almost always marked with が, because it describes an unfolding event, not a topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は is strongly dispreferred inside this kind of adverbial clause; it would try to pull 話 out as a sentence-level theme, which the structure doesn't allow.

contrast_examples.jp: 時が経つにつれ、傷は癒えた。
contrast_examples.en: As time passed, the wound healed. (subordinate が)
This story is long. (main-clause topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 寺カフェに着いた圭介の様子を見た弥子について。
prompt.prompt_jp: カウンター越しの弥子___すぐに彼の表情の陰りに気づいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this already-known character acting?

feedback.correct_en: Yako is already an established character; the sentence picks her up as the topic and reports what she did. Topic-continuation like this takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would feel like Yako was being introduced for the first time or singled out as THE one who noticed, neither of which matches the flow.

contrast_examples.jp: 弥子はすぐに気づいた。
contrast_examples.en: Yako noticed right away. (known actor — は)
It was Yako who noticed. (identificational — が)

prompt.context_jp: サイン会当日、書店の前の様子。
prompt.prompt_jp: 駅前の書店には長蛇の列___伸びていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the line in this scene-setting line?

feedback.correct_en: A long line is being newly presented to the reader as part of the scene. New-information existence with 伸びていた takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the long line' feel like something already known that we're now commenting on, which doesn't match this first glimpse of the venue.

contrast_examples.jp: 店の前に行列ができていた。
contrast_examples.en: A line had formed in front of the store. (new scene — が)

contrast_examples.jp: その行列は、三時間待ちだった。
contrast_examples.en: That line had a three-hour wait. (now topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: ついに圭介の順番が回ってきた瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 出雲凛音の顔___、思っていた以上に幼かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this commentary on the author's face?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence takes 出雲凛音の顔 as its topic and compares it against Keisuke's expectation — a contrastive/topical reading that calls for は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the face as new information in an all-focus statement, which doesn't fit a line evaluating the face against prior expectation.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の顔は、意外に幼かった。
contrast_examples.en: Her face was surprisingly young-looking. (topic comment — は)
A young face came into view. (new perception — が)

prompt.context_jp: 吉原が自分の過去を語り始める。
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕には 学生時代からの夢___ありました。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks what he had?

feedback.correct_en: With ある describing possession/existence, the thing that exists is introduced with が. The dream is new information in his confession.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would contrast this dream with some other dream, which isn't what he's doing. を can't appear with ある.

contrast_examples.en: I have a dream. (existence — が)

contrast_examples.jp: その夢は叶わなかった。
contrast_examples.en: That dream didn't come true. (now topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 吉原が憑依の瞬間について語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の消えたいという気持ちと 僕の生きたいという気持ち___ あのとき リンクした。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the paired subjects of リンクした?

feedback.correct_en: He is naming exactly these two feelings as what connected — an identificational/exhaustive statement about the subject of リンクした, which takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize the two feelings and expect a comment about them, but the sentence instead reports the specific event of their linking.

contrast_examples.jp: 二つの思いがつながった。
contrast_examples.en: The two feelings connected. (event — が)

contrast_examples.jp: 二つの思いは、別々のものだ。
contrast_examples.en: The two feelings are separate things. (topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 静まり返った部屋で、他に音がない情景。
prompt.prompt_jp: 匙を動かす音だけ___、しばらく部屋を満たしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle follows だけ here?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけ picks out the sole thing filling the room, and such 'only X and nothing else' subjects use が — an exhaustive-listing reading.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜だけは would shift the meaning to 'at least that one thing...' — a contrastive concession, which doesn't match the still, singular image here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の声だけが聞こえた。
contrast_examples.en: Only his voice could be heard. (exhaustive — が)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の声だけは覚えている。
contrast_examples.en: His voice is the one thing I remember. (contrastive — は)

prompt.context_jp: USJの思い出で盛り上がる四人を描いた地の文。
prompt.prompt_jp: 血の繋がりを超えた「家族」という言葉___、この輪では自然に口にされるようになっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this reflective, topical sentence?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator pulls 「家族」という言葉 out as the topic and reflects on how it has come to be used — a textbook topic-comment structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the word as a fresh event-participant, but the sentence is clearly a meta-observation about a theme the chapter has been building.

contrast_examples.en: The word 'family' is a heavy one. (topic — は)

contrast_examples.jp: 「家族」という言葉が聞こえた。
contrast_examples.en: I heard the word 'family'. (new perception — が)

prompt.context_jp: この十年、圭介の過ごし方について。
prompt.prompt_jp: この十年、圭介がこの部屋で年___越すのを避けてきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 越す here?

feedback.correct_en: 年を越す ('see out the year') is a fixed transitive collocation — 年 is the direct object, so を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark 年 as a subject, but 越す here is transitive. に would wrongly suggest a destination of movement.

contrast_examples.en: To see in the new year with family. (fixed を-collocation)
To cross over a mountain. (same を-pattern)

prompt.context_jp: 本に挟まれていたメモの一行。
prompt.prompt_jp: 地下のカフェ___きて
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the destination in this invitation?

feedback.correct_en: 来る expresses movement toward a goal; the arrival point is marked with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would describe a location where an action takes place, not where someone is coming to. を doesn't work with 来る for a destination.

contrast_examples.en: Come to my place. (destination — に)
Let's have tea at my place. (location of action — で)

prompt.context_jp: 食後、貴恵が圭介にちょっとばつが悪そうに言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: お正月早々 迷惑___ちゃったわね。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes the natural collocation with 迷惑?

feedback.correct_en: 迷惑をかける ('to cause trouble for someone') is the standard set collocation and fits her apologetic tone perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 迷惑をやる or 迷惑を出す are not idiomatic in Japanese — speakers would never phrase this that way.

contrast_examples.jp: ご迷惑をおかけしました。
contrast_examples.en: I apologize for causing you trouble. (polite set phrase)
Don't be a nuisance to others. (same collocation)

prompt.context_jp: 友利が凛音に電話しようとスマホを取り出した場面の地の文。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___は急げと、友利はスマートフォンを取り出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes this proverb?

feedback.correct_en: 善は急げ ('do a good thing without delay') is a well-known proverb matching Tomori's eager impulse to call right now.
feedback.incorrect_en: 命は急げ and 時は急げ aren't fixed proverbs. The learner may be thinking of 時は金なり, which has a different form entirely.

contrast_examples.en: Strike while the iron is hot. (set proverb)
Time is money. (different proverb)

prompt.context_jp: 心配しすぎる圭介と麻衣にあきれる貴恵。
prompt.prompt_jp: いちいち ___なのよ 約束したでしょ 私たちは家族だって。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures her light annoyance at them overreacting?

feedback.correct_en: 大げさ ('making too big a deal of it') perfectly matches her chiding them for panicking over a moment that passed.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大事 ('important/precious') would praise them, not scold them. 大変 ('terrible/a lot') describes a situation, not a person's reaction style.

contrast_examples.en: Don't blow it out of proportion.
It's an important matter.

prompt.context_jp: 娘を見つめながら貴恵が笑って言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: ホントに 世話___焼ける娘だこと。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes the set expression 'a handful of a child'?

feedback.correct_en: 世話が焼ける is the fixed intransitive form meaning 'troublesome / needs looking after'. The subject (世話) takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 世話を焼く is a related but different idiom meaning 'to look after (someone)'. Here the predicate is 焼ける (intransitive), so を doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: He's a handful. (intransitive — が)
To take care of my little sister. (transitive — を)

prompt.context_jp: 凛音に相手にされなかった圭介と友利に貴恵があきれて。
prompt.prompt_jp: ホントに 頼り___ならない男たちね。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes 'unreliable men'?

feedback.correct_en: 頼りになる / 頼りにならない is the fixed pattern for 'reliable / unreliable'. The に marks the result-state after なる.
feedback.incorrect_en: 頼りがならない and 頼りをならない are not idiomatic. Learners sometimes default to が for subjects, but this is a に+なる state expression.

contrast_examples.en: He's reliable. (fixed pattern)

contrast_examples.jp: こいつは頼りにならない。
contrast_examples.en: This guy is unreliable.

prompt.context_jp: 帰りの車内、友利が沈黙を破って励ますように言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: こんな不思議な現象の説明なんて そもそも ___られないよな。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'can't give an explanation'?

feedback.correct_en: 説明をつける / 説明がつく is the standard collocation for 'to come up with / give an explanation'. 'つけらんない' is the casual negative potential.
feedback.incorrect_en: 説明を出す isn't an idiomatic pairing in Japanese. 説明を見る is literally 'to look at an explanation', not 'to produce one'.

contrast_examples.en: There's no explaining it.
To make the story add up. (same つける pattern)

prompt.context_jp: お年玉を渡した貴恵が麻衣に軽く言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 出どころは 私の五百円玉貯金だから 気遣いは___よ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes 'no need to worry about it'?

feedback.correct_en: 気遣いは無用 ('no need to worry about it') is a slightly stiff set phrase that fits Takie's dignified-wife register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 無理 means 'impossible/forced' and would warp the meaning. 無事 means 'safe/unharmed' and doesn't pair with 気遣い.

contrast_examples.en: There's no need to worry.
That's impossible.

prompt.context_jp: ぼうっとしている圭介に貴恵が指示を出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: ほら 圭介 みんなの分 コーヒー___ちょうだい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb form fits 'make coffee for everyone'?

feedback.correct_en: コーヒーをいれる is the idiomatic verb for brewing/pouring coffee or tea. It's the natural choice in a casual home context.
feedback.incorrect_en: 作る is understandable but less natural for coffee — it suggests something more like making a dish. 焼く ('to grill/bake') doesn't fit coffee at all.

contrast_examples.en: I'll make us some tea.
To cook a meal.

prompt.context_jp: 吉原の言葉を思い出す貴恵の心の中で響く一文。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the most natural, weighty way to express 'what is borrowed must one day be returned to its rightful owner'?

choices.text: 借りたものは いつか返さなきゃいけない 本当の持ち主に
いつか借りたものを本当の持ち主は返さなきゃいけない
本当の持ち主に借りたものはいつか返さなきゃいけない

feedback.correct_en: Option A places 借りたものは up front as the topic and tails 本当の持ち主に as a reflective afterthought — a dramatic, pause-and-add rhythm that fits a line of quiet realization.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B scrambles the subject and makes 本当の持ち主 the topic, which changes the meaning. Option C is grammatical but loses the heavy, trailing emphasis that the scene depends on.

contrast_examples.jp: 借りたものは返す、必ず。
contrast_examples.en: What is borrowed, we return — without fail. (trailing-emphasis style)

contrast_examples.jp: 必ず借りたものは返す。
contrast_examples.en: I will always return what I borrow. (flat, less dramatic)

prompt.context_jp: 弥子が圭介のため息を数えてからかう場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Yako's teasing line?

choices.text: 新島さん ため息つくの
新島さんがため息をつくことの
新島さんは ため息のつき方を

feedback.correct_en: Option A's casual noun-phrase ending ('you sighing, that is') lands naturally after her prior line '7回目' — colloquial, playful, and complete without a full predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B over-nominalizes with ことの and feels bookish. Option C turns it into a comment on his 'way of sighing', which isn't what she means.

contrast_examples.jp: それ、三回目。あくびするの。
contrast_examples.en: That's your third one — yawning, I mean. (casual noun phrase)

contrast_examples.jp: あくびをするのが三回目です。
contrast_examples.en: That is your third yawn. (stiffer, full-predicate)

prompt.context_jp: 整理券が一枚しかない場面で、圭介が決意して言う。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally conveys Keisuke's firm, slightly stiff resolve?

choices.text: いや 僕に行かせてくれ 僕が話をする
いや 僕を行くようにしてくれ 僕は話をあげる
いや 僕も行かれて 僕を話す

feedback.correct_en: 〜に〜せてくれ is the natural pattern for 'let me (do X)', and 話をする is a standard collocation. The result is firm, unaffected adult speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: B mangles the causative into 行くようにしてくれ and uses 話をあげる, which isn't a real collocation. C uses the passive 行かれて incorrectly and drops を on the wrong noun.

contrast_examples.jp: 僕に行かせてください。
contrast_examples.en: Please let me go.
I'm the one who'll do the talking.

prompt.context_jp: 弥子が「いくら丼」のたとえで圭介を励ます。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best fits Yako's lively, metaphor-driven speech style?

choices.text: “なくなっちゃう なくなっちゃう”って食べてたら せっかくの うまい いくら丼の味 分かんなくない？
喪失の予期の下で摂食した場合、当該丼の美味を認識することは不可能である。
なくなっちゃうなくなっちゃうということを言いながら食べてしまうならば、せっかくの美味であるいくら丼の味は分からないのではないか。

feedback.correct_en: Option A's casual 〜って, 分かんなくない？, and sound-reduced tone match Yako's warm, slangy café register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is written-academic register — totally wrong for café chat. C is grammatical but formal and stiff, nothing like the way Yako actually teases Keisuke.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなの、楽しめなくない？
contrast_examples.en: You wouldn't even enjoy it that way, right? (casual tag question)

contrast_examples.jp: そうした場合、楽しむことはできない。
contrast_examples.en: In such a case, one cannot enjoy it. (formal)
